independent_reasoning: For finite J and finite real weights/node values, each Q(u psi_alpha) is a finite real sum because the finite polynomial basis has finite values at finite real nodes. The finite estimated polynomial is then an element of the admitted finite basis span, regardless of whether u itself is globally measurable/integrable/square-integrable. No integral of u is used by these formulas.

The actual def-finite-chaos-orthogonal-projection begins For real u in L2(rho). Its exact coefficient pairing is legitimate because each admitted psi_alpha is in L2(rho), and its own declared Cauchy-Schwarz interface makes the product integrable. Its orthogonal projection language concerns this real L2 quotient and finite space. Merely having finitely many real node values cannot supply the missing global hypothesis.

For a concrete counterexample compatible with the support convention, let rho be uniform on[0,1], choose admissible constant basis psi0=1, and take u(y)=1/y for y>0, defining u(0)=0. At finitely many interior nodes u is finite, so the estimator is finite. On each interval (2^(-k-1),2^(-k)] the integrand u is at least2^k and the interval length is2^(-k-1), so every such interval contributes at least1/2 to its nonnegative integral. Thus the exact constant coefficient diverges. The finite estimator still makes sense and is intentionally retained.

The actual weighted orthogonal-polynomial Galerkin definition was also inspected: it explicitly places V_N(mu) inside L2(mu), defines L2 by finite squared-integral classes, and defines its spectral projection on admissible coefficient sequences. It does not license arbitrary node-evaluable projections. It is not a direct dependency of the chaos estimator, so no supplier change or new edge is proposed.

No duplicate algorithm, new lemma, new result or native-creation record is needed: this is a precise conditional interpretation within the existing definition. Empty Lambda and zero/empty cubature sums retain their finite algebraic meanings; the conditional exact projection notation stays on its established L2 domain.
